newsitem.title: USA: NJ group proposes utility deregulation by mid-1998.
newsitem.headline: NJ group proposes utility deregulation by mid-1998.

text.p: The New Jersey Coalition for Customer Choice said it wants state regulators to approve restructuring of New Jersey's electric utilities no later than June 1998.

The group represents some of the participants in Energy Master Plan discussions held at the request of the New Jersey Board of Public Utilities, including two of the electric utilities -- GPU Inc and Atlantic Energy Inc.
The state's largest electric utility, Public Service Enterprise Group Inc, also participated in the talks, but is not a member of the coalition.
Other members of the coalition are KCS Energy Inc, the Chemical Industry Council of New Jersey, Independent Energy Producers of New Jersey, New Jersey Food Council and New Jersey Retail Merchants.
Having reached "consensus positions on several key policy points," the group said, it decided to present these views to the board.
Its "members support an open retail competitive marketplace as the vehicle to achieve (their) goals" -- lowering electric rates in the state and promoting New Jersey's economic progress.

The coalition calls for securitization of stranded costs, advocating state authorization of a revenue stream through the purchase of bonds securtized by a stranded cost recovery charge -- which would be based on a calculation including investments in the test year of each utility's last approved base case.
"Any costs incurred after the date of the last base rate case ... should be subject to a market test," the group said.

Its position statement also also said the board "must address the percentage -- if any -- of stranded cost recovery that the utilities must share with ratepayers" in establishing a market transition charge to recover approved costs.
The coalition said it believes "the sanctity of contracts with non-utility generators should be recognized ... and the costs of these contracts fully recoverable from ratepayers."
It went on to seek incentives to mitigate those costs.
It also called for establishment of incentives for utilities to divest power generating facilities.

The group said recovery of costs other than stranded costs, such as demand management and social programs, should not be met through bonding. But these should be shown separately on bills as part of an unbundling of rates.
